shared_elements: bilateral symmetry about a vertical central axis
justification: Both are stone surfaces worked in low relief with an insistent bilateral symmetry around a vertical axis, and both include disc-like roundels and horizontal banding, which is the most specific correspondence. The biggest difference is format and density: A is a flat, framed rectangular panel packed edge-to-edge with small narrative figures in crisp, fine-line carving, whereas B is a massive three-dimensional standing figure carrying only a few large, shallow, weathered motifs on its body.
